rooster noun

also cock, cockerel, crow (of a rooster), cock-a-doodle-doo

classical

Traupman 141, 143–144

gallus, gallī m.

noun, second declension

rooster, cock

Other words

  • cūcūriō, cūcūrīre — crow (of a rooster)

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · late Latin · Auct. Carm. Philom. 25 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 372

Examples

  • Gallus canit: surgendum est.

    The rooster is crowing: time to get up.composed

  • Gallī cūcūriunt (canunt).

    Roosters crow.Traupman 372

See also hen, crow.

SourcesLewis & Short: gallus · Lewis & Short: cucurio

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 141, 143–144.
